title: The Afternoon Brief: BC wildfire grows past 39 sq mi as House faces funding choice
dek: The Bald Range wildfire expanded further overnight as British Columbia's state of emergency took effect, while Congress confronts competing funding bills and Netanyahu publicly rejected Trump's Gaza plan hours before the midday news cycle closed.
author: GoCheckMyNews
key_fact: The wildfire has grown to over 39 square miles with more than 20,000 evacuated and a state of emergency now granting provincial authorities expanded powers; the House must choose between the Senate's bipartisan continuing resolution and its own GOP measure to avert a fiscal shutdown; and Netanyahu's explicit rejection of Trump's 15-point Gaza proposal signals a widening breach between the Israeli and U.S. administrations.
bottom_line: Three separate crises moved forward midday: the BC wildfire expanded past 39 square miles with a state of emergency now in effect; Congress faces a funding choice as Senate and House bills diverge; and Netanyahu publicly rejected Trump's Gaza plan, widening a breach with the U.S. administration weeks before Israeli elections. Watch for the House's decision on government funding, updated containment figures from BC, and whether Trump or his team formally responds to Netanyahu's conditions.
body: The Bald Range wildfire in British Columbia has continued its rapid expansion since the morning edition, now spanning more than 39 square miles across Summerland, Peachland, and surrounding districts. British Columbia declared a state of emergency Saturday afternoon, granting the province special powers to restrict travel and secure accommodations for the more than 20,000 evacuees already ordered from their homes. The fire, which doubled in size since Friday, generated its own weather system and lightning according to reporting, and remains out of control amid more than 100 active wildfires across the province in conditions officials describe as unusually intense. The state of emergency underscores the velocity of the threat: the growth from the morning's 36 square miles to the afternoon's 39 square miles, combined with the province's declaration of expanded emergency authority, reflects how quickly conditions have escalated.

On the fiscal front, the Senate's 90-6 vote Saturday morning to approve a continuing resolution funding the government through December 11 now moves the choice to a House that passed a separate GOP-led measure before its August recess. That bill faced Democratic opposition, creating a direct collision between two versions and leaving Speaker Johnson to decide which path avoids a shutdown at the September 30 deadline.

In the Middle East, Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu made explicit what had been implicit: he publicly rejected President Trump's 15-point Gaza peace proposal Saturday at a Cabinet meeting, stating Israel will not withdraw from Gaza until Hamas is completely disarmed. Hamas reaffirmed its commitment to the Trump plan and called on mediators to pressure Netanyahu to comply, according to the reporting. The rejection marks a direct breach between Netanyahu's political constraints and Trump's negotiation timeline, occurring weeks before Israeli elections set for October.

The reporting does not yet establish what ignited the Bald Range wildfire or confirm structure losses from the blaze. The House's decision on the competing funding bills remains the near-term fiscal checkpoint.
